current_activity: Tractable: attacks towards the Laison on the left of the Canadian columns to protect their flank
notes: Event date: 14 August 1944, noon (Ellis, vol. I, pp. 425, 430). Event definition: At noon on 14 August the division of I Corps, on the left of the 3rd and 4th Canadian Divisions, attacks towards the Laison to protect the Canadian flank; it had come back under I Corps with the 33rd Armoured Brigade when the inter-corps boundary was swung south during the four days of the earlier Canadian attack, 7-10 August (p. 425; Stacey dates it 9 August, CR0852). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 430: "At the same time the 51st Division of I Corps, on their left, also attacked towards the Laison to protect the Canadian flank"; p. 425: "I Corps had taken the 51st Division and 33rd Armoured Brigade under command again". Location: Soignolles, Calvados (new place), the Canadian start line with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is Soignolles on the Caen-Falaise road; the division attacked on the left, some miles to the east. Location support: Ellis places the Canadian start line on either side of Soignolles and the 51st Division on its left (p. 430); no closer place is given for the division.

current_activity: Le Havre: joins the assault from the north at midnight; clears the Montgeon forest, Octeville and the high ground
notes: Event date: 11 September 1944 (from midnight on the 10th) (Ellis, vol. II, pp. 14, 15). Event definition: At midnight on 10 September, using artificial moonlight, the division and the 33rd Armoured Brigade join the I Corps attack on Le Havre on the right of the 49th Division, attacking from the north; the minefields and the anti-tank ditch are crossed by early morning, and by the end of 11 September the division has cleared the Montgeon forest, taken Octeville, cleared the high ground nearly to Cap de la Heve and forced its way into the outskirts of Le Havre to attack Fort St. Addresse (pp. 14-15). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 14: "using artificial moonlight,2 the 51st (Highland) Division and the 33rd Armoured Brigade came in on their right attacking from the north"; p. 15: "Meanwhile the 51st Division had cleared the Montgeon forest, taken Octeville". Location: Le Havre, France (existing place PL0169) with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is the town of Le Havre, the objective; the division fought on the north side and its headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis names Le Havre as the objective and the places cleared (pp. 14-15). Review (British Batch 2, 28 October 2026; inferred value; old value: operation_id OP-CAMP-NORTHERN-FRANCE; new value: operation_id OP-ASTONIA): the row is part of the I Corps assault on Le Havre of 10 to 12 September 1944, which Stacey, p. 331, calls a neat and expeditious three-day operation in the second week of September and names Operation Astonia; the new operation is a child of OP-CAMP-NORTHERN-FRANCE, so the narrower operation replaces the broader one. The other rows under OP-CAMP-NORTHERN-FRANCE are not about Le Havre.

current_activity: Ardennes: relieves the 53rd Division at Grimbiemont on the 8th; secures Laroche on the 11th
notes: Event date: 11 January 1945 (Ellis, vol. II, pp. 190, 191). Event definition: The division relieves the 53rd Division at Grimbiemont on 8 January; on 9 January the Germans start to vacate their most westerly positions and on the 11th the division secures Laroche; resistance then stiffens again, but the western branch of the Ourthe river is reached on the 13th and next day contact is made with the reconstituted American VIII Corps attacking from the south (pp. 190-191). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, pp. 190-191: "where they were relieved on the 8th by the 51st Division"; "on the 11th the 51st Division secured Laroche". Location: La Roche-en-Ardenne, Luxembourg province (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location approximate: the point is the town centre of La Roche-en-Ardenne (Laroche in Ellis); the division headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis names Laroche as the town secured (p. 190).
